source.title: On the geometry and topology of representations: the manifolds of modular addition
source.authors: Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja; G. McCracken; Harley Wiltzer; Vincent Létourneau; Colin Daniels; D. Precup; J. Love

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures representation geometry and phase-alignment distributions across modular-addition architectures and training runs using PCA, topological summaries, and distributional distances, rather than the original sources' methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports qualitative PCA structures for selected circuits and evaluates gradient symmetricity and distance irrelevance as architecture diagnostics. Those are not direct measurements of cross-model representation alignment, so they are not rows here. The PAD distributions, torus-distance comparisons, and cross-seed Betti-number results are recorded.
record.test_reason: The study compares learned representations across four architectures (MLP-Add, uniform-attention, trainable-attention, MLP-Concat) and hundreds of seeds on modular addition. It uses phase-alignment distributions, torus distance, PCA and persistent homology to ask whether the same circuit or representation recurs. That bears directly on universal circuits (V5) and on cross-seed convergence (V3). Because the same pairs are scored under several summaries, it also bears on measure dependence (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the Clock and Pizza (uniform vs trainable attention) architectures learn topologically and geometrically equivalent representations and the same algorithm. They say all studied architectures, including MLP-Concat, factor one torus-to-logit map, with some learning lower-rank linear projections (discs) of the torus. This restores universality for modular addition, and the analysis is limited to that task.
record.recipe_differences: Uses learned phase distributions, PCA, MMD, torus distance, and persistent homology to compare modular-addition representations; it does not reproduce the original studies' representation-alignment recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: PAD estimates (maximum activation versus center of mass) and representation summaries (PAD MMD versus torus-distance MMD) yield different distance magnitudes. Persistent homology uses a fixed k-nearest-neighbour setting of 250.
record.problems: The experiments concern only modular addition and do not vary task data or objectives, so they cannot identify shared data or objectives as a cause. There is no model-scale or capability sweep. Distributional comparisons are statistically significant even where the authors describe the distributions as close. The persistent-homology neighbour setting is fixed, and the paper notes that persistent homology can miss small-radius holes.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep; cross-architecture similarity is measured only on tiny modular-addition models.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation transfer between models.
No SAE features or large models; the only task is modular addition.
The persistent-homology k (fixed at 250) is not varied, and there are no out-of-distribution inputs.
No manipulation of shared data or objectives, and no plateau analysis. Incomplete alignment is recorded under V5 limits_scope.

missing.what: PCA variance of first-layer frequency clusters: MLP-Add, Pizza and Clock have more than 99% of variance in 2 PCs (disc). MLP-Concat has 4 PCs at about 25% each (torus). This shows a shared representation for three architectures.

MMDs on Zhong et al.'s gradient symmetricity and distance irrelevance. Attention 0.0 vs 1.0 gives 0.7750 and 0.2078 (very strong/moderate difference), whereas the PAD MMD is 0.0338. The pair's similarity therefore depends on the metric.
Betti-number percentages per architecture, layer and depth (e.g. share of seeds yielding a disc or torus in layer 1).

record.verdict_notes: The V6/V7 links on all MMD rows were replaced by V5 links, with V6 kept only for the MLP-Add vs attention cross-summary contrast. V7 has no rows because causes are untested. Inconsistencies in the paper: §6.1 cites Table 2 for PAD MMDs, but these are in Table 1. The Fig. 5 caption gives attention-pair MMDs (0.0237/0.0181) that differ from Table 1 (0.0338/0.0210). Table 2 uses 512-neuron models and 2000 samples, while Table 1 uses 1024-neuron models and 20,000 samples, which confounds the measure comparison. Every difference is statistically significant, and 'nearly the same' is the authors' reading.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size, capability, or alignment as models scale.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
The study measures phase distributions and manifold topology, not shared features or subspaces across seed-specific models.
No mapping between model representations, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
It compares several representation summaries and two phase estimators, but does not vary the persistent-homology k-nearest-neighbour setting or test out-of-distribution inputs.
It studies architectures trained on the same modular-addition task; it does not manipulate shared data or objectives, test other tasks, or assess convergence plateaus.
